I need to write a test class for SoundexUtils, a package-private class in org.apache.commons.codec.language, so the test must live in the same package. I'm analyzing the branches in the clean(String str) method: null input returns null, empty string returns as-is, and otherwise it loops through characters checking Character.isLetter.

For difference(StringEncoder, s1, s2), I need an actual Soundex encoder implementation since StringEncoder is just an interface. This is Defects4J Codec-1b, so Soundex, StringEncoder, and EncoderException should already exist in the same project and compile together, even if the given classpath libraries don't explicitly list commons-codec.jar.

I could either use the real Soundex implementation directly, or better yet, build a fake anonymous StringEncoder to isolate testing of difference() from Soundex's own logic.

For differenceEncoded(), I need to cover null handling for either or both encoded strings, and test the character-matching loop against edge cases like empty strings, equal strings, mismatched lengths, and full/no matches. Now I'm setting up the test class file with the package declaration and imports.

Adding clean() test cases...

Adding more test cases...

Adding more difference test cases...

Finishing the null encoder test, verifying it returns 0 as expected. Now I need to double-check the actual method signatures on the commons-codec StringEncoder and Encoder interfaces to make sure my implementation matches correctly.

This confirms encode(String) resolves correctly and returns String, satisfying the type match I need. I check that the null-encoding test case returns 0 when either encoded string is null, and verify my anonymous class correctly overrides both encode(Object) and encode(String) so it compiles properly.

Now I trace through the SoundexUtils.clean tests: empty strings return the same reference, all-letter strings uppercase correctly, mixed letter/digit strings extract only letters, and no-letter strings return empty. I'm working through the spaces-and-punctuation case, extracting just the letters from "Hello, World!" to confirm it produces "HELLOWORLD".

Then checking the difference-encoded tests, I catch an error: comparing "W123" vs "W124" character by character, the first three positions match but the last digit doesn't, so the correct diff count is 3, not 2 as I'd assumed. I need to fix the expected value in that test and the related difference() test to use 3 instead of 2.

The other length-mismatch tests still hold at 2 and 1 respectively, and the identical/no-match cases at 4 and 0 also check out. I just need to update the code for the mismatched cases.

I'm deciding not to test against the real Soundex class directly since it's outside scope, sticking with the fake encoder to keep tests isolated and avoid dependency issues.

I still need to cover the edge case where one string is empty and the other isn't, since lengthToMatch would be zero there too but through a different path than the both-empty case. Adding a test for differenceEncoded with an empty string and a non-empty string to confirm the loop is skipped and diff stays zero.

Now I'll finalize the test file, double-check the anonymous StringEncoder implementation compiles correctly with proper imports, and put together a summary table mapping methods to their covered branches.
